get.summary: Estimate the resident population exposed around a place
get.description:
Estimate, for an arbitrary radius, the resident population around a place.

The figure is an **estimate of exposure**, produced by areal weighting of
CPV 2024 DEGURBA units: each overlapping unit contributes its population in
proportion to the share of its own area inside the buffer. It is not a count
of people present, and it is not a casualty figure. The declared spatial
assignment rule and both standing assumptions are returned with it, because
the figure cannot be interpreted without them.

The cached estimate on ``GET /places`` uses the default radius; this endpoint
recomputes for the radius asked for, which costs roughly 40 ms.

parameters.name: radius_meters

schema.description: Radius in metres. The place location is a GEOGRAPHY point, so the buffer is metres on the ground, not degrees.

get.summary: Rank every district by the PRIO-SV Vulnerability dimension
get.description:
Rank the 262 districts by the Vulnerability dimension of PRIO-SV.

The score is the equally weighted geometric mean of two sub-dimensions,
each normalised by the CDC/ATSDR SVI 2022 percentile method with equal
weights at variable level and no PCA. It is a **relative rank among
Salvadoran districts** and nothing else.

The response carries the declared data gaps, because half of this dimension
is a measurement and half is a proxy: the vulnerable-groups sub-dimension
rests on five measured district rates, while the socioeconomic
sub-dimension rests on a single territorial proxy, since the ingested
corpus publishes no CDC socioeconomic variable at district level and the
construction-material tables were not ingested at all.

get.summary: Apply the district Vulnerability score to the DEGURBA polygons
get.description:
Attribute each district's Vulnerability score to its DEGURBA sub-districts.

The score is **measured at district level** and attributed to the finer
polygon, which assumes vulnerability is uniform within the district. That is
the same assumption place exposure already makes when it applies district
vulnerable-group rates to a DEGURBA population, and it is returned with the
result because the figure cannot be read without it.

Nothing here is measured at sub-district level: a DEGURBA polygon has no age
pyramid, no disability count and no household composition of its own.

schema.description: Restrict the result to one six-character district code.

get.summary: Retrieve every variable behind one district's Vulnerability score
get.description:
Take one district's Vulnerability score apart into the variables behind it.

Returns every declared variable's raw estimate (``E``), rate (``EP``) and
percentile rank (``EPL``), each sub-dimension's percentile sum (``SPL``) and
rank (``RPL``), both composition rules, and every withheld cell with the
bound on what its absence can cost. A score nobody can take apart cannot be
defended in front of an emergency committee or a jury, which is the whole
reason this endpoint exists.

get.summary: Rank every district by the PRIO-SV Lack of Coping Capacity dimension
get.description:
Rank the 262 districts by the Lack of Coping Capacity dimension of PRIO-SV.

Higher is worse: 10 means "worst placed of the 262 districts on this
method". The score is normalised by the CDC/ATSDR SVI 2022 percentile method
with equal weights at variable level and no PCA, then composed by INFORM
2017's geometric mean.

Two things in the response are not optional reading. Every distance is a
**geodesic straight line and a lower bound on travel distance** -- pgRouting
is not installed, so nothing here is a route. And the **institutional
sub-dimension is a declared gap**, because no published subnational DRR
capacity indicator exists for El Salvador, so this dimension is
infrastructure only and its score equals its infrastructure score.

get.summary: Per-polygon access measurements behind each district's LCC score
get.description:
Return the per-polygon distances a district's LCC figure averages.

Unlike the Vulnerability dimension, LCC's underlying measurement really is
taken at this finer level: each DEGURBA Nivel 2 polygon has its own measured
distance, and the district figure is their population-weighted mean. A
district whose urban core sits 400 m from a clinic and whose rural fringe
sits 12 km away publishes one number, and an operator deciding where to send
a brigade needs the spread rather than the average.

The attributed ``score`` is still the district's, under the uniformity
assumption returned with the response.

get.summary: Retrieve every variable behind one district's LCC score
get.description:
Take one district's LCC score apart into the variables behind it.

Returns every declared variable's raw estimate (``E``), rate (``EP``) and
percentile rank (``EPL``), each sub-dimension's percentile sum (``SPL``) and
rank (``RPL``), both composition rules, and the four context variables that
are measured and published but deliberately excluded from the index, each
with the evidence that excluded it. A score nobody can take apart cannot be
defended in front of an emergency committee or a jury, which is the whole
reason this endpoint exists.

get.summary: Rank every district by the composed PRIO-SV index (baseline or event)
get.description:
Composed PRIO-SV ranking. The response always declares its mode.

Baseline answers "where would a disaster hurt most"; event answers "who to
attend first" for one ShakeMap grid. Sphere minimum requirements are
attached to naranja and roja districts in event mode. No figure is a
casualty count, and the ranking is of territories, not people.

parameters.name: event_id

schema.description: USGS event id (e.g. usp000a9jv). Omit for BASELINE mode (V x LCC, no event). Supply it for EVENT mode (H&E x V x LCC) against that event's ShakeMap.

PlaceExposureEstimateRead.description:
Areal-weighted **estimate** of the resident population around a place.

None of these numbers is a count of people present. They estimate how many
residents the CPV 2024 census places inside ``radius_meters`` of this point,
and the census records where people live, not where they were when an event
happened. ``null`` means withheld under statistical secrecy or outside census
coverage; it never means zero.
